newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Commerzbank profits up, asserts independence.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Commerzbank profits up, asserts independence.

text.p: Germany's Commerzbank AG on Tuesday reported a 50 percent jump in nine month pre-tax profits and insisted it would remain an independent player in a market widely seen as heading for consolidation.

Strong growth in interest and commission income enabled the bank to lift pre-tax profit to 1.675 billion marks ($1.1 billion), up from 1.125 billion in the same period last year and up 40 percent from the entire 1995 result of 1.19 billion marks.
Commerzbank is the last of the "Big Three" Frankfurt banks to publish nine-month results and, as expected, managed to outshine its two larger rivals in terms of earnings growth.
Germany's biggest bank Deutsche Bank and Dresdner Bank had already reported nine month figures.

Chief executive Martin Kohlhaussen seized on the result to counter recent market speculation that Commerzbank may become one of several banks to face merger or takeover in Germany's overcrowded banking market.
"We won't buy anyone and there is no danger that we will be acquired," Kohlhaussen told a news conference.

Commerzbank's heavy market capitalisation of 15 billion marks should deter potential bidders, he said, adding that he could not imagine a buyer paying that kind of money for a branch retail network in need of restructuring.
Kohlhaussen reiterated that Commerzbank did not plan to raise its dividend for 1996 from the 13.50 marks paid for 1995.
He predicted the bank would post a "satisfactory" result for 1996, which would enable it to pay a dividend while strengthening bank reserves.
Operating profit after provisions rose 36.9 percent to 1.67 billion marks compared with the year-ago period, below analysts' expectations for a figure of 1.8 billion marks.

The slowdown in operating profit growth from a 47.6 percent rise posted after the first six months was partly explained by disappointing own-account trading income in the third quarter, Commerzbank said.
Unsuccessful share trading performance meant trading profits were up just 11.4 percent at 402 million marks in the first nine months after jumping 45 percent in the first half.
But the bank said trading profit would pick up in the final quarter when capital gains would be realised.

Analysts said Commerzbank's results were positive overall and said its rivals had not fared much better on trading income in the first nine months. Commerzbank's shares closed post-bourse trade up 0.13 marks at 34.04.

The bank said that given an expected tax ratio of around 40 percent, after-tax profit was roughly one billion marks, which translates into a return-on-equity of just over 11 percent after tax and 18.7 percent before tax.
Risk provisions also rose, to a net level of 658 million marks from 562 million, reflecting continued need for caution given steadily rising insolvencies in Germany, the bank said.
Kohlhaussen stressed that while the bank did not plan to dismantle its cost-laden domestic retail branch network it would continue to merge unprofitable branches.

Meanwhile the bank's telephone banking subsidiary Comdirect was developing well and had attracted more than 64,000 customers since it was formed in 1995 -- more than any other telephone bank in Germany, Kohlhaussen said.

Reacting to the relaxation of shop closing hours which came into force on November 1, some 100 Commerzbank branches would stay open longer in future, Kohlhaussen said. Deutsche and Dresdner have already announced similar moves.

Operating expenses rose 7.3 percent to 4.16 billion marks. Group lending grew 12.7 percent to 293.4 billion marks. The balance sheet total climbed 7.6 percent to 434.7 billion marks. ($ = 1.51 German Marks)
